name: The Karmelicka Elm
verified_sources: GDOS pomniki przyrody register (gid 72149, kodinspire PL.ZIPOP.1393.PP.1261011.970), designated 1998-11-16

pl.wikipedia.org Pomniki przyrody w Krakowie wykaz table, entry 71: ul. Karmelicka 51, girth 290 cm, designated 1997, CRFOP id .970 (matches GDOS record). Table states 'as of 2023' and explicitly excludes trees delisted in earlier years, so this entry is a 2023 living-tree confirmation.
access: Free, roadside tree on public ground (ul. Karmelicka), open at all hours
transport: About 12-15 minute walk from Rynek Glowny (Main Square); near the Nowy Kleparz market area
story:
Elms are the trees Europe mostly lost, which is why a protected one standing on a working Krakow street is worth the quarter hour it takes to walk out from the Main Square. This is a European white elm, wiaz szypulkowy in Polish, on the pavement outside ul. Karmelicka 51 in Piasek, a few streets west of the Planty ring. Its trunk measures 290 centimetres around.

The species belongs to wet ground, river floodplains and old flood terraces rather than dry city verges. It gives itself away in early spring, before the leaves: the flowers and then the seeds hang out on long stalks, which is what the Polish name records, and every flat seed case is fringed with fine white hairs.

Poland's national register dates the protection to 1998. The city's own published list says 1997. Both entries carry the same register number and the same girth, so what disagrees is a year on paper rather than the identity of the tree.

Nobody has recorded its age. The register holds a girth and an address and nothing else, and no other dated white elm in this city offers anything to measure it against. If you know when this one went into the pavement, tell us.

name: The Morawskiego Elm
verified_sources: GDOS pomniki przyrody register (gid 72033, kodinspire PL.ZIPOP.1393.PP.1261011.1112), designated 1987-06-09

pl.wikipedia.org Pomniki przyrody w Krakowie wykaz table, entry 49: ul. Morawskiego 5, girth 399 cm, designated 1997, CRFOP id .1112 (matches GDOS record). Same 2023-snapshot table that excludes prior delistings.
access: Free, roadside tree on public ground (ul. Morawskiego), open at all hours
transport: About 13-16 minute walk from Rynek Glowny (Main Square), on the west side toward Zwierzyniec/Salwator
story:
At 399 centimetres round, this is the thickest elm on this list, and the two sources describing it cannot agree on when Poland decided to protect it. The national register says 1987. The city's own published list says 1997. Both quote the same register number and the same girth to the centimetre, so this is one tree wearing two dates, and the decade between them is a slip in somebody's transcription rather than a question about which elm is meant.

It is a European white elm at ul. Morawskiego 5 in Zwierzyniec, the quarter that runs west from the Old Town toward the Vistula and the Kosciuszko Mound, about fifteen minutes from the Main Square on foot. Four metres of circumference works out at a trunk roughly 127 centimetres across, which is a lot of elm to meet on a residential street anywhere in Europe. Of the continent's native elms, this is the species that the bark beetles carrying Dutch elm disease tend to pass over.

Nobody has dated it. No planting record exists, and no comparable dated white elm stands in this city to measure the girth against, so the register's protection year is the oldest fixed point there is. If you know when it went in, tell us.

name: The Pilsudskiego Lime
age_estimate: roughly 130 years, estimated from its girth against Krakow's other register limes
verified_sources: GDOS pomniki przyrody register (gid 71967, kodinspire PL.ZIPOP.1393.PP.1261011.1039), designated 2013-12-14

pl.wikipedia.org Pomniki przyrody w Krakowie wykaz table, entry 252: ul. Pilsudskiego 29, girth 339 cm, designated 2013, CRFOP id .1039 (matches GDOS record), with its own Commons photo (Small-leaved linden (Tilia cordata Mill.), 29 Pilsudskiego street, Krakow, Poland.jpg).
access: Free, roadside tree on public ground (ul. Pilsudskiego), open at all hours
transport: About 10-12 minute walk from Rynek Glowny (Main Square), toward Blonia park
story:
Krakow did not put this lime on its register of natural monuments until December 2013, by which time it had been standing on ul. Pilsudskiego for well over a century. Nothing records the planting. What exists is a tape measure: 339 centimetres round.

That number can be read here, because two other small-leaved limes on this page come from the same register and were dated the same way. Krowoderska is 402 centimetres and reads as 130 to 175 years, Tarlowska is 259 and reads as 85 to 115. Slotting 339 between them gives roughly 110 to 150 years, an estimate taken off a trunk rather than a birth date, and the width of the band is the honest shape of that arithmetic.

Three lime species stand on this page, so it is worth knowing which one you have. Small-leaved lime carries the smallest leaf of the group, heart-shaped and blue-green underneath with rust-coloured tufts of hair in the vein angles. The silver lime on ul. Kosciuszki flashes white undersides in wind, and the large-leaved lime on ul. Daszynskiego has a bigger leaf, soft with hairs.

It stands on the way down to the Blonia, about seven hundred metres from both the Straszewskiego Ash and the Kosciuszki Silver Lime, so it joins a loop rather than making a trip of its own.

best_time.label: late June into July, when the flowers open and the crown fills with bees you can hear from the pavement

name: The Strzelecki Garden Plane
age_estimate: roughly 170 years, estimated from its girth against Krakow's other register planes

location.address: Ogrod Strzelecki, ul. Lubicz 16, Wesola, Krakow

verified_sources: GDOS pomniki przyrody register (gid 72047, kodinspire PL.ZIPOP.1393.PP.1261011.858), designated 1966-12-16

pl.wikipedia.org Pomniki przyrody w Krakowie wykaz table, entry 53: Park Strzelecki / Ogrod Strzelecki, girth 420 cm, designated 1997, CRFOP id .858 (matches GDOS record), with its own Commons photo (Platanus acerifolia, Strzelecki Garden, 16 Lubicz street, Krakow, Poland.jpg).
access: Free, public park (Ogrod Strzelecki), open at all hours
transport: About 13-15 minute walk from Rynek Glowny (Main Square); close to Krakow Glowny main railway station
story:
Krakow's main railway station has an old plane tree for a neighbour, 420 centimetres round, standing in a park most arriving passengers walk straight past. The Ogrod Strzelecki is a public garden beside the nineteenth-century hall of the city's marksmen's society, about a quarter of an hour east of the Main Square on foot.

The two lists that carry the tree disagree on when it was protected. The national register says December 1966, the city's own published list says 1997. Same register number, same girth to the centimetre, so this is one tree with two dates on it rather than two trees.

Its age comes off the trunk, because nothing records a planting. This page already carries two other London planes measured by the same register: the Filharmonia Plane at 520 centimetres, read as 150 to 270 years, and the Studencka Plane at 315 centimetres, read as 90 to 165. Placing 420 between them gives roughly 120 to 220 years. The band is wide on purpose, since a plane in a city grows at whatever rate the city allows it.

The species is a seventeenth-century hybrid, oriental plane crossed with American sycamore, and it turned out to tolerate soot, paving and hard pruning better than anything else on offer. That is why it lines streets from London to Krakow, and why one of them ended up shading a garden next to a railway terminus.

name: The Wola Justowska Oak

location.address: ul. Dunin-Wasowicza / ul. Lowiecka, Wola Justowska, Krakow

verified_sources: GDOS pomniki przyrody register (gid 145734, kodinspire PL.ZIPOP.1393.PP.1261011.2846), designated 2016-01-06

pl.wikipedia.org Pomniki przyrody w Krakowie wykaz table, entry 266: ul. Dunin-Wasowicza/ul. Lowiecka, girth 351 cm, designated 2015, CRFOP id .2846 (matches GDOS record), with its own Commons photo (Krakow ul. Lowiecka pomnik przyrody Dab szypulkowy Quercus robur.jpg).
access: Free, roadside tree on public ground at the Dunin-Wasowicza/Lowiecka junction, open at all hours
transport: About 15-18 minute walk from Rynek Glowny (Main Square), in Wola Justowska toward Las Wolski
story:
This is one of the newest names on Krakow's monument register, a list whose earliest entries reach back to the 1960s. The national record enters the oak in January 2016, the city's own list says 2015, and the two agree on everything else, including a trunk of 351 centimetres.

It stands at the junction of ul. Dunin-Wasowicza and ul. Lowiecka in Wola Justowska, the villa district on the western edge of the city, on the way out to the woods of Las Wolski. That is about twenty minutes on foot from the Main Square and a little off the run of the other trees here, so treat it as its own stop rather than a link in a chain.

Pedunculate oak is named for its acorns, which hang out on long stalks while the leaves sit almost flat against the twig with two small lobes curling back at the base like ears. It is also the oak of Polish national memory, the species behind Bartek and the Rogalin veterans.

Nobody has recorded its age. No planting record survives for a suburban junction, and the other register oaks in this city carry no age either, so there is nothing local to measure 351 centimetres against. Someone who has lived on that corner for fifty years knows more than the register does. If that is you, tell us.

best_time.label: September into October, when the acorns come down and roll across the junction

name: The Botanical Garden Hungarian Oak

location.address: ul. Kopernika 27, Ogrod Botaniczny Uniwersytetu Jagiellonskiego, Wesola, Krakow

verified_sources: GDOS pomniki przyrody register (gid 177905, kodinspire PL.ZIPOP.1393.PP.1261011.2879), designated 2017-02-07

pl.wikipedia.org Pomniki przyrody w Krakowie wykaz table, entry 282: ul. Kopernika - Ogrod Botaniczny, girth 462 cm, designated 2017, CRFOP id .2879 (matches GDOS record), with its own Commons photo (Krakow ul. Kopernika 27 Pomnik przyrody Dab wegierski Quercus frainetto.jpg).
access: Paid entry, Jagiellonian University Botanical Garden (open seasonally, check hours)
transport: About 17-19 minute walk from Rynek Glowny (Main Square)
story:
The Hungarian oak is a tree of the Balkans and the Carpathian basin, and Krakow sits several hundred kilometres north of anywhere it grows on its own. This one, inside the Jagiellonian University's Botanical Garden, measures 462 centimetres round and joined Poland's register of natural monuments in February 2017.

Dab wegierski is the Polish name for it. The leaf is the giveaway, and the reason to look up rather than at the trunk: among the largest of any European oak, half again as long as the pedunculate oak leaves elsewhere on this page, cut into many narrow lobes and bunched toward the ends of the shoots.

The garden around it was founded in 1783 and is the oldest in Poland, and this corner of it holds an unusual concentration of old trees. The Jagiellonian Oak, the oldest confirmed black locust in the country and the Sniadecki dogwoods all stand within a couple of hundred metres of it, which makes one ticket buy four entries on this page.

Nothing records when the oak went in, and no other dated tree of its species in Poland gives a way to read that girth, so the age stays open rather than guessed at. The garden charges admission and keeps seasonal hours, so check them before making the twenty minute walk east from the Main Square.

name: The Botanical Garden Canary Palm

location.address: ul. Kopernika 27, Ogrod Botaniczny Uniwersytetu Jagiellonskiego (winter greenhouse), Wesola, Krakow

verified_sources: GDOS pomniki przyrody register (gid 145180, kodinspire PL.ZIPOP.1393.PP.1261011.2845), designated 2014-12-03
pl.wikipedia.org Pomniki przyrody w Krakowie wykaz table, entry 264: ul. Kopernika 27 - Ogrod Botaniczny, girth 172 cm, designated 2014, CRFOP id .2845 (matches GDOS record)

krakow.pl official city tourism page on the Jagiellonian University Botanical Garden (fetched directly, not from a search summary): 'najstarsza w Polsce palma - daktylowiec kanaryjski Phoenix canariensis, znajdujacy sie w szklarni zimowej, miejscu letnich koncertow' (the oldest palm tree in Poland, a Canary Island date palm, standing in the winter greenhouse, a venue for summer concerts).
access: Paid entry, Jagiellonian University Botanical Garden, inside the winter greenhouse (open seasonally, check hours)
transport: About 17-19 minute walk from Rynek Glowny (Main Square)
story:
Poland's oldest palm tree lives indoors in Krakow, in a greenhouse used for concerts in summer. The city's own tourism pages give the title to this Canary Island date palm in the winter house of the Jagiellonian University's Botanical Garden.

It has been a protected natural monument since December 2014, with a stem 172 centimetres round. That figure will not date it, and nothing else does either. Palms have no cambium and lay down no annual rings, and the trunk reaches close to its final thickness early and then goes up rather than out, so the tape measure that dates the oaks and limes on this page is no use at all here.

Phoenix canariensis comes from the Canary Islands and would not last a Krakow February outdoors, which is the entire reason it is under glass. It is one of two trees on this page you visit with a roof over your head, the other being the cycad in the palm house nearby. Entry is ticketed and the glasshouses keep their own hours, which are worth checking before the walk out.

Nobody publishes a planting year. The garden and the city both call it the oldest in the country and stop there. If you have seen a date on a label or in a garden catalogue, tell us and we will add it.

name: The Botanical Garden Cycad
age_estimate: at least 162 years, recorded at the garden since 1864

location.address: ul. Kopernika 27, Ogrod Botaniczny Uniwersytetu Jagiellonskiego (palm house), Wesola, Krakow

verified_sources: GDOS pomniki przyrody register (gid 145179, kodinspire PL.ZIPOP.1393.PP.1261011.2844), designated 2014-12-03

pl.wikipedia.org Pomniki przyrody w Krakowie wykaz table, entry 265: ul. Kopernika - Ogrod Botaniczny, girth (stem) 108 cm, designated 2014, CRFOP id .2844 (matches GDOS record), with its own Commons photo

krakow.pl official city tourism page (fetched directly): 'najstarsza kolekcja sagowcow z okazem sagowca zwinietego Cycas circinalis notowanym juz w 1864 r. Wizerunek tego kwitnacego co roku okazu stanowi logo ogrodu' (the oldest cycad collection [in Poland], with a specimen of Cycas circinalis already recorded in 1864; the image of this specimen, which flowers every year, is the garden's own logo).
access: Paid entry, Jagiellonian University Botanical Garden, inside the palm house (open seasonally, check hours)
transport: About 18-20 minute walk from Rynek Glowny (Main Square)
story:
The botanical garden's logo is a portrait of one of its own residents, and this is the resident: a Cycas circinalis under glass in the palm house of the Jagiellonian University's Botanical Garden, part of what the city calls the oldest cycad collection in Poland.

It was recorded here in 1864. That is a first mention rather than a planting date, which makes it a floor and not an age: at least 162 years on this site, and probably more, since the record marks when somebody wrote the plant down rather than when it started growing. No source offers an upper figure, so none is given here.

A cycad is not a tree and is not closely related to one. The lineage was already old when the first flowering plants appeared, and what looks like a trunk is a caudex, a squat storage column that thickens very slowly. The register measures it at 108 centimetres round, a number that stands for a great deal of time rather than for a large plant.

The garden says it flowers every year, which for a cycad means a cone rather than a blossom, and it is that annual performance that put the plant on the institution's own letterhead.
